CT-skanning is a diagnostic imaging procedure that serves as a central element in the Danish national quality standards for acute abdominal surgery. It is the primary focus of [[indikator-2|Indikator 2]], which measures the timing of the procedure, specifically defining the time limit for execution after hospital arrival to two hours (120 minutes) [^src1]. 

The procedure is deeply integrated into the clinical and logistical workflows of acute care. In the 2024 Akut Kirurgi Databasen (AKDB) report, policy decisions regarding treatment timelines reflect the practical challenges of acute surgery. For example, the time limit for antibiotic treatment, monitored by [[indikator-1|Indikator 1]], is maintained at three hours after arrival. This threshold is deliberately set as a trade-off to avoid delaying the CT-skanning, illustrating the logistical balancing act required when prioritizing diagnostic imaging alongside medical interventions [^src1]. These indicators are part of a broader quality development effort aimed at reducing mortality and improving treatment standards through evidence-based, measurable goals, while adjusting targets based on clinical realities and new studies like AHA and ELPQUICK [^src1].
